This is a nonpersonal services contract requesting software development of Autonomy Government Reference Architecture (A-GRA) interfaces for the Mission Termination System (MTS), yielding a Technology Readiness Level 9 (TRL 9) product . MTS is a Run Time Assurance (RTA) tool based on the Testing Autonomy in Complex Environments (TACE) code base created by Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Lab (JHU APL). MTS is used at Edwards AFB to safely test autonomous control of small Unmanned Aerial Systems (sUAS). The government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the contractor who, in turn, is responsible to the government. 1.1.1 Description of Services/Objectives. The contractor shall provide all management, personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportatio

ion. 1.6.3 Delivered product shall integrate A-GRA autonomy interface into the existing MTS Service Set creation tool. It will draw them in and build on the knowledge and skill acquired in each stage. Programme Aim The purpose of this training programme is to design, develop and deliver a training programme that build people’s understanding of self-harm and the role it plays in the life of a person who self-harms. The programme will build the knowledge and confidence of the learner to have a conversation if they are concerned that someone may be self-harming. The training programme should provide people who access it with a sense of hope and reassurance that people can build healthier coping mechanisms. Programme Objectives The training programme is intended to: Increase understanding of what self-harm is. Increase understanding of the relationship between self-harm and suicide. Build skills and confidence to engage with a person and speak openly about self-harm. Challenge the stigma surrounding self-harm Increase awareness of available supports and services Stage 1: An introduction to the subject of self-harm – communicating the ‘why’ functions of self-harm through lived experience experts.
